title: Reflection automorphism from a locally nilpotent rational sl2 action
statement:
Let $L$ be a rational Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra], not necessarily finite-dimensional. Let $\mathfrak t\subseteq L$ be an abelian subalgebra, $h\in\mathfrak t$, $e,f\in L$, and $\alpha:\mathfrak t\to\mathbf Q$ linear. Assume $\alpha(h)=2$, $[e,f]=h$, $[t,e]=\alpha(t)e$ and $[t,f]=-\alpha(t)f$ for every $t\in\mathfrak t$. Assume $\operatorname{ad}e$ and $\operatorname{ad}f$ are locally nilpotent: for every $x\in L$ some power of each operator annihilates $x$. For $D=\operatorname{ad}e$ or $-\operatorname{ad}f$, define $\exp(D)x=\sum_{n\geq0}D^n(x)/n!$, a finite sum for each $x$. Then
$$w=\exp(\operatorname{ad}e)\circ\exp(-\operatorname{ad}f)\circ\exp(\operatorname{ad}e)$$
is a rational Lie algebra automorphism and satisfies
$$w(t)=t-\alpha(t)h\quad(t\in\mathfrak t),\qquad w(e)=-f,\quad w(f)=-e.$$
For a linear functional $\beta:\mathfrak t\to\mathbf Q$ write $L_\beta=\{x\in L:[t,x]=\beta(t)x\text{ for all }t\in\mathfrak t\}$. The automorphism restricts to an isomorphism
$$w:L_\beta\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\beta-\beta(h)\alpha}.$$
No decomposition of $L$ into weight spaces is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504, Lie-theoretic reflection input to the Serre presentation; rational-field applicability stated on p.508. The expanded locally-nilpotent exponential argument is agent-supplied; Serre, Complex Semisimple Lie Algebras, Chapter VI, appendix, is WANTED.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{ad}e$ and $G=-\operatorname{ad}f$. Jacobi and bilinearity in [def-wf-lie-algebra] give $E[x,y]=[Ex,y]+[x,Ey]$ and the same identity for $G$. The assumed local nilpotence of $\operatorname{ad}f$ implies that of $G$, since $G^nx=(-1)^n(\operatorname{ad}f)^nx$. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-nilpotent-derivation-exponential] to $E$ and $G$. Thus $A=\exp E$ and $B=\exp G$ are rational Lie automorphisms, so is $w=ABA$, and $w^{-1}=A^{-1}B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, pp.503-504; rational extension p.508. Agent-supplied local-exponential and sl2 reflection calculation.

proof.text:
For $t\in\mathfrak t$ write $a=\alpha(t)$. The brackets give $Et=-ae$, $Ee=0$, $Ef=h$, $Eh=-2e$; also $Gt=-af$, $Ge=h$, $Gf=0$, $Gh=-2f$. Consequently the finite sums are
$$A(t)=t-ae,\quad A(e)=e,\quad A(f)=f+h-e,\quad A(h)=h-2e,$$
$$B(t)=t-af,\quad B(e)=e+h-f,\quad B(f)=f,\quad B(h)=h-2f.$$
For example $E^2f=-2e$, $G^2e=-2f$, and all subsequent terms vanish. The relations with $h$ use $h\in\mathfrak t$ and $\alpha(h)=2$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, pp.503-504; rational extension p.508. Agent-supplied local-exponential and sl2 reflection calculation.

proof.text:
Compose these formulas in the stated order. For $t\in\mathfrak t$,
$$BA(t)=t-ae-ah,\qquad ABA(t)=(t-ae)-ae-a(h-2e)=t-ah.$$
Similarly $BA(e)=e+h-f$ and $A(e+h-f)=e+(h-2e)-(f+h-e)=-f$; while $BA(f)=f+(h-2f)-(e+h-f)=-e$ and $A(-e)=-e$. This proves all three displayed reflection formulas, and in particular $w(h)=-h$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, pp.503-504; rational extension p.508. Agent-supplied local-exponential and sl2 reflection calculation.

proof.text:
Define $s:\mathfrak t\to\mathfrak t$ by $s(t)=t-\alpha(t)h$. Since $\alpha(h)=2$, $\alpha(s(t))=-\alpha(t)$ and $s(s(t))=t$. The preceding formula gives $w|_{\mathfrak t}=s$, hence also $w^{-1}(t)=s(t)$. If $x\in L_\beta$, bracket preservation gives
$$[t,w(x)]=w([s(t),x])=\beta(s(t))w(x)=(\beta(t)-\beta(h)\alpha(t))w(x).$$
Thus $w(L_\beta)\subseteq L_\gamma$ for $\gamma=\beta-\beta(h)\alpha$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, pp.503-504; rational extension p.508. Agent-supplied local-exponential and sl2 reflection calculation.

proof.text:
For $y\in L_\gamma$ put $z=w^{-1}(y)$. Then
$$[t,z]=w^{-1}([w(t),y])=\gamma(s(t))z.$$
Here $\gamma(h)=-\beta(h)$, so $\gamma(s(t))=\gamma(t)-\alpha(t)\gamma(h)=\beta(t)$. Therefore $z\in L_\beta$. These restrictions of $w$ and $w^{-1}$ are inverse rational linear maps between the indicated weight spaces (subspaces by bilinearity). This proves the asserted isomorphism, including zero weight spaces, without a weight-space decomposition of $L$.
